title: Spread difficulty across easy, medium and hard
statement: Spread a test's items across easy, medium and hard, since an all-medium form puts weak students at the floor and strong ones at the ceiling.
example: One adaptive engine serves only hard items from a score of 90, so an all-medium bank leaves it nothing to serve there.
detail: The staged assessment standard fails an all-medium form because it disables discrimination, putting weak readers at the floor and strong ones at the ceiling, and requires a spread across easy, medium and hard (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/docs/standards/assessment-design.md`). The course checklist adds that all-medium items silently disable adaptivity (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/CHECKLIST.md`), since the adaptive engine it targets chooses difficulty by the current score: easy from 0 to 49, medium and hard at 75% and 25% from 50 to 89, and hard only from 90 to 99 (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0054-reference.qmd`).

evidence.quote: A 100%-medium form **disables discrimination** — it floors weak readers and ceilings strong ones, measuring nothing. The form **must spread** across easy / medium / hard.
items carry easy/medium/hard (NOT 100%-medium) so PowerPath can ease/ramp. *(new — 100%-medium silently disables adaptivity)*
difficulty by current score (0–49 easy; 50–89 medium+hard 75%/25%; 90–99 hard only)
1. Measure students across the full G2–G5 ability range (RIT 161–227) in 40 items
